column3: Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “clothes” as “garments.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text (“I will make”) and omits “answering.”
NASB omits the first “behold” and renders “in whom” as “with whom.”
NASB adds “to the ground” and has no “greatly.”
NASB adds “to them.”

Close to the Greek.
Close to the Greek; NASB has “His disciples,” with “His” as in the Textus Receptus.
NASB follows the critical text without “Jesus” and “first.”
NASB renders “from them” as “at their hands.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB supplies “Jesus” and moves “and saying” from v. 15 into this verse.
NASB renders “epileptic” (literally “moonstruck”) as “a lunatic” and “suffers miserably” as “is very ill”; “saying” is moved to v. 14.
Close to the Greek.
“Until when” is rendered “how long,” and “bear with” is “put up with.”
“From that hour” is rendered “at once.”
“Cast out” is rendered “drive out.”
NASB follows the critical text with “littleness of your faith”; “as a mustard seed” becomes “the size of a mustard seed.”
This verse is absent from the critical text; NASB prints it in braces, following the Textus Receptus.
NASB follows the critical text with “gathering together” (Textus Receptus: “abiding”); “betrayed” is rendered “delivered.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “didrachmas” as “the two-drachma tax.”
NASB renders “anticipated him” as “spoke to him first” and “tribute” (census tax) as “poll-tax.”
NASB follows the critical text (“When Peter said”) and renders “free” as “exempt.”
NASB renders “four-drachma coin” (stater) as “a shekel.”
